approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a persistent tree of molecular graph edits and purchases the selected frontier molecule directly. Accepted scores update the exact traversed occurrences, which retain completed returns, their best observed return and outstanding purchases. After an accepted improvement, it starts fresh ordered roots at the current and preceding incumbents using their original scored receipts. Each promoted root is valued by its own best return, while molecular similarity still shares completed and pending counts between the roots for exploration. The initial forest and deeper choices retain shared peak values and counts.
approach.novelty: Remove only the completed-count borrowing between promoted roots when computing their exploration bonus and zero-start priority. Each root will use its own completed count plus the existing shared pending count. This isolates a remaining exploration consumer after the Parent already removed peak-value borrowing. Earlier controls removed root value and both densities together, or changed completed density deeper in a different tree composition; the parallel sibling removes pending borrowing instead. None answers this completed-count question on the own-value two-root Parent.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-fc3b91c9623a converts own-root peak allocation into a complete mean 0.5001487124432433 (SD 0.01368931088288767), +0.019178652901946685 versus its code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8, but late incumbent-increment mass falls from 0.8656010443094923 to 0.8438973049856529 and the formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains 0.1068816037678877 higher. The limiting behavior addressed here is completed-count borrowing continuing to suppress exploration independently of those now-own-root values. Independent read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent Search logs in policy/scratch/r0058-01-improve-L01/audit-summary.json verifies 7484/7484 promoted-root rows have D>N. Changing only the consumer denominator D+P to N+P increases all those bonuses and changes 2076/3742 same-state root choices, all from current to preceding origin, in fourteen cells. Those changed decisions lie on 1989/4350 actual paid paths and 1239/2175 late paths, with zero formula/trajectory-join mismatches; median_2 seed 0 never promotes and remains included. Each per-cell audit cites and hashes its underlying Parent logs, trajectories, summary and run.log. Exposure is not utility. n-51af92d7316d jointly removed value and both densities, while n-f86545a81e31 removed deeper completed density under shared value on a fresh-single-root host; neither supplies this conditional contribution sign.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen search-policy-r58-conditional-credit-and-optimality-probability review only as context for separating completed and pending counts. Retain the inherited actual pending accounting and parent numerator. Execute the internally evidenced N+P consumer removal under the literal frozen conditions; do not implement WU-UCT anew, RAVE, qPO, a new density estimator or another control.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen planning review distinguishes actual completed/pending accounting from synthetic cross-origin density. This ticket introduces no paper mechanism: the code Parent already implements actual N/W/M/O, shared D/P, own-root peak value and the two-root lifecycle. Its actual logged row replay and unresolved conditional contribution gap justify removing only completed cross-origin support from the existing exploration consumer. Neither WU-UCT theory nor RAVE supplies this molecular conditional sign; no new source recipe, model, code release or package is adopted.

sources.applicability: Useful separation of actual pending evidence from completed rewards. The inherited molecular sibling-smoothed counts are an adaptation; neither the paper guarantee nor actual-pending utility establishes cross-origin shared-density utility.

hypothesis: Remove off-diagonal completed density solely from the promoted-root exploration and zero-start consumer, on n-fc3b91c9623a and only when episode > 0 and parent_id == 0. For root i, keep D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j and P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j stored/computed exactly as before, but let active_started_i=N_i+P_i instead of D_i+P_i. Active exploitation remains M_i if N_i>0, otherwise the inherited neutral default. For positive active_started_i, bonus_i=beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/active_started_i), with beta 0.5; at zero preserve the inherited unvisited-priority handling. Use the unchanged earliest-occurrence winner rule. The mechanism is removal of another origin's completed support from this one consumer, not removal of pending support, value normalization elsewhere, actual receipt credit or widening.

finding_summary.headline: Completed-density removal changes paid search but refutes non-inferiority; retaining it helps on this host
finding_summary.insights: The arithmetic and paid behavioral prediction happened; the registered expectation that this removal would be non-inferior did not. The result supports positive conditional contribution of shared completed exploration density when promoted roots use their own accepted-return peaks and still share pending density. It preserves the earlier value-only result and says nothing additive about pending density, deeper sharing or two-root membership. This is a scientific utility refutation, not an execution failure or a verdict on the whole tree-search approach. The controller bought 1,589 preceding-origin descendants instead of 785 and 1,991 current-origin descendants instead of 2,795. Preceding-origin increment mass rose from 0.27218464819532534 to 1.4796325349706514, while current-origin mass fell from 3.6563807047140133 to 2.3565875773939475. These descriptive allocations show that extra access and extra local peak renewals can coexist with lower total conversion; they do not identify which alternative purchase would have won. Most of the task-mean loss came from sitagliptin_mpo (-0.05076437433620579) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.01585388776582025), partly offset by drd2_docking (+0.03304154036490403). The chemistry does not support a simple scaffold-collapse diagnosis. Typed/generic scaffold unions increased from 1,684/1,188 to 1,811/1,288, while the fragment-excluded within-session count-Morgan similarity remained nearly unchanged (0.22278266458637686 to 0.22272000697904817). Fewer below-six-heavy-atom purchases (306 to 251) coexisted with more above-fifty purchases (289 to 314). The molecular assessment finds diverse ring chemistry but inconsistent preservation of useful connected ring, amine and carbonyl relationships, alongside reactive heteroatom combinations and unspecified stereochemistry. Thus broader coverage and fewer fragments alone did not solve useful conversion. A proposal operator that preserves rewarded connected structural relationships during topology changes, or a search scheme that values expected further progress rather than peak renewal alone, could address that limitation; neither is tested here. No surrogate-ranking diagnosis is available because this active controller has no learned surrogate. Controlled runtime effects, safety, mediation and transfer beyond this finite Search panel remain open.

Changed choices reached 1,158 of 4,350 paid molecules, including 717 of 2,175 late purchases. Fourteen task/seed cells were exposed; the never-promoted median_2 seed-0 session remained exactly unchanged. Source and receipt checks found no isolation, arithmetic, credit or purchase-join discrepancy. The mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.5001487124432433 to 0.493992363073594, a paired change of -0.006156349369649354. This crosses the registered -0.002 utility falsifier. Seed mean changes were +0.012008293955467986, -0.017959810390718034 and -0.012517531673698012; six task/seed endpoints improved, eight worsened and one tied. Total incumbent-increment mass fell from 4.37484902101401 to 4.282503780469271 even though strict improvements rose from 142 to 150. Late mass rose from 0.8438973049856529 to 1.2676125536333678, with 38 to 55 improvements, so improved late activity did not recover the lost full-budget endpoint performance. The formal Anchor mean remained 0.607030316211131, a separate deficit of 0.11303795313753702.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich carbonyl heterocycles, cyclic amines and N/O cages coexist with reactive bonds, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assesses output of n-bf023e9ce9f8 against published code Parent n-fc3b91c9623a on the frozen epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch ten. The exact frozen context states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. All fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectory files exist and were read; no task or matched Parent cell is missing. All 4500 accepted rows per side were inspected; descriptor denominators are 4350 optimizer proposals per side, excluding 150 fixed initial observations. Rejected or unpurchased graphs are not represented. The Child contains substituted aromatic carbonyl heterocycles, fused diones, aryl-bearing saturated amines, and heteroatom-rich partly saturated cages. There are 3990 ring-bearing and 3386 aromatic-atom-bearing proposals, versus Parent 3905 and 3288. Digest ring-closure-token rates span 0.8966 to 0.9437 and aromatic-token presence rates 0.4529 to 0.9115; these are string presence rates, not atom fractions. Conventional amines, ethers, esters, amides and carbonyls coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, hydrazine/thiocarbonyl combinations and crowded rings. Thus rich ring chemistry and broad graph diversity do not establish uniformly plausible synthesis. Child heavy atoms span 1 to 118, median 26, versus Parent 1 to 114, median 26. Full below-six/above-fifty tails are 251/314 versus 306/289. Late optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 retain all 2175 purchases per side, with tails 116/211 versus 143/179. Fewer fragments coexist with more large assemblies; a useful size range is not universal. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold panel unions are 1811/1288 versus 1684/1188; late unions are 1075/813 versus 972/724. Sums of within-cell full distinct scaffold counts are 2026/1584 versus 1898/1485, a different statistic from panel unions. Individual upper neighborhoods remain related despite broad panel diversity. Fragment-excluded within-cell sparse count-Morgan Tanimoto means are 0.22272000697904817 versus 0.22278266458637686, over 558314 versus 543335 unordered pairs. Late means are 0.2664520661001478 versus 0.27268294975031904 over 140454 versus 136877 pairs. These are pair-weighted means with at least six heavy atoms, radius two, no chirality, and no cross-task or cross-seed pairs. The companion 2048-bit Morgan means are 0.20048381730232023 versus 0.20202255305312944, and late 0.24211722371280636 versus 0.2532065461147983. Bit statistics match the descriptor family in the Parent molecular report; sparse count statistics are separately recomputed on both panels and are not substituted for that historical definition. Under current broad atomic-number bond flags, O-O/O-halogen/N-halogen union counts are 967 versus 1022, with late counts 565 versus 619. Child individual flag counts are 191/586/225 versus 264/679/176. These current flags include aromatic heteroatoms and any bond order; they differ from the earlier Parent report's SMARTS flags, whose counts remain unchanged in its source. They are structural alerts, not measured stability, toxicity or synthetic accessibility. Every optimizer string in both panels lacks @ tokens, while matched current RDKit perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2364 Child and 2437 Parent proposals. Neutral Child strings still contain protonatable-looking amines; charge notation does not measure basicity. Scores below are copied from accepted trajectories. They do not disclose a target pharmacophore, binding pose, synthesis route or stereoisomer preference. Last purchases are not necessarily final incumbents. No mechanism activation, component attribution, safety, independent replication or runtime claim is made. Formal Anchor trajectories were not part of this matched chemistry audit. Provenance and definitions: policy/scratch/r0058-01-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json, policy/scratch/r0058-01-improve-L01-molecular/source-map.json, and policy/scratch/r0058-01-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json. The source map pairs every per-cell audit with the underlying Search input and its hash. Original Child paths are request-authorized staging files outside the run; immutable in-run copies preserve those bytes for audit and are not a published node archive. Published Parent chemistry history was read at nodes/n-fc3b91c9623a/molecular.json, with historical descriptor definitions and provenance at policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json and policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/source-map.json; its original comparison with n-b13ef5ae4ba8 is retained as historical context, not relabeled as the present comparison.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
